acquisition method: Acquisition was performed in data-dependent acquisition (DDA) mode
alkylation reagent: alkylated in the dark with 60 nmol iodoacetamide (25°C, 30 min)
alkylation concentration: alkylated in the dark with 60 nmol iodoacetamide (25°C, 30 min) and alkylated in the dark with 180 nmol iodoacetamide (30 min at 25°C)
cleavage agent: digestion with endoproteinase LysC (1:10 LysC weight: Cell lysate weight, overnight at 37°C; Wako, cat # 129-02541) and then diluted 2-fold with 200 mM ammonium bicarbonate for trypsin digestion (1:10 w:w, 8 h at 37°C; Promega, cat # V5113)
collision energy: Fragment ion spectra were produced via collision-induced dissociation (CID) at normalized collision energy of 35%
fragmentation method: Fragment ion spectra were produced via collision-induced dissociation (CID) at normalized collision energy of 35%
instrument: Samples were analyzed using a LTQ-Orbitrap Velos Pro-mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, San Jose, CA, USA)
ionization type: positive ionization mode with nano spray
The mass spectrometer was operated in positive ionization mode with nano spray voltage set at 2.1 kV
labeling: we performed free-label mass spectrometry analyses of M. agalactiae and M. pneumoniae to obtain a quantitative proteome overview of both species
reduction concentration: reduced with 30 nmol dithiothreitol (37°C, 60 min) and alkylated in the dark with 180 nmol iodoacetamide (30 min at 25°C). Following the filter-aided sample preparation (FASP) method described in, samples were then digested with 3 μg LysC (Wako, cat # 129-02541) overnight at 37°C, and then with 3 μg of trypsin (Promega, cat # V5113) for eight hours at 37°C. After digestion, peptide mixes were acidified with formic acid and desalted with a MicroSpin C18 column (The Nest Group, Inc) prior to LC-MS/MS analysis. Samples with SDS lysis buffer were reduced with 90 nmol dithiothreitol (30 min at 56°C)
